events.title: A Giant Spider!
events.body: A giant spider has moved into the clubhouse. It is wearing a tiny scarf in club colors.

outcomes.text: The spider becomes the club's famous mascot. Supporters share spider memes, pack the stands, and copy its tiny scarf.
The spider vanishes before its mascot debut. The internet remains unmoved.
The groundskeeper calmly relocates the spider and shares a few useful training tips.

events.title: A Meteor Shard!
events.body: A warm blue stone is humming in the center circle. The groundskeeper insists it was not there yesterday.

choices.label: Put it in the trophy case

outcomes.successHeadline: The queue goes round the block
outcomes.text: The shard becomes a glittering local attraction and fans queue around the block.
It cools into a perfectly ordinary rock. The trophy cabinet looks embarrassed.
A delighted geology department pays promptly and promises not to ask about the scorch mark.

events.title: Training in a Lightning Storm
events.body: The squad votes to keep training while purple lightning marches toward the ground.

outcomes.text: Every strike lands in rhythm with the drill. The squad finishes crackling with confidence.
The floodlights explode. Training ends with eleven people hiding under one tiny dugout.
Bert serves tea while the storm waters the pitch for free.

events.title: Mysterious Energy Drink
events.body: A salesman in mirrored glasses offers one unlabelled crate and refuses to blink.

outcomes.text: The squad trains at impossible speed and alphabetizes the cones before cooling down.
It tastes like warm cucumber. Everyone spends the afternoon burping in unison.
The salesman vanishes. One useful cooler remains behind.

events.title: The Abandoned Lab
events.body: A team-building bus takes a wrong turn and stops outside a laboratory marked DEFINITELY EMPTY.

outcomes.text: The motion sensors wake up and award the club a research grant for excellent footwork.
The only discovery is a vending machine that accepts coins but gives nothing back.
The driver finds the training camp. Nobody mentions the moving curtains.

events.title: Radioactive Pitch Repaint
events.body: The bargain line-marking paint glows beautifully after sunset and faintly during lunch.

outcomes.text: Night matches become famous. Supporters arrive in glow paint and never miss a line call.
The league inspector arrives wearing three dosimeters. Emergency repainting is not cheap.
The pitch returns to an entirely reassuring shade of green.

events.title: A Very Old Boot
events.body: A mud-caked boot falls from a sealed loft. It fits every player perfectly.

outcomes.text: Every shot curls into the top corner. The boot earns its own velvet cushion.
Every shot hits the same corner flag. The boot is returned to the loft facing the wall.
The club historian identifies it as old, important, and extremely smelly.

events.title: Team BBQ
events.body: The captain volunteers to cook for everyone despite owning a single enormous spatula and no thermometer.

outcomes.text: The feast is magnificent. Even the substitutes receive ceremonial grilled onions.
The burgers are technically charcoal. Team bonding happens over takeaway menus.
Nobody gets famous, sick, or hungry. A professional success.

events.title: Prank War
events.body: Every training cone has been replaced by a tiny traffic cone wearing a moustache.

outcomes.text: Your remote-controlled tactics board wins the war and the dressing room erupts.
Your fake team sheet reaches the local paper. Bert spends all morning making corrections.
The moustached cones are retained for morale purposes.

events.title: The Mascot Is Missing
events.body: The mascot costume is gone. A trail of oversized footprints leads toward the high street.

outcomes.successHeadline: A parade all the way home
outcomes.text: The mascot leads a spontaneous parade back to the ground with hundreds of new supporters.
It was in the laundry room. The search party still submits mileage claims.
A giant pencil entertains the crowd and asks to keep the shirt.

events.title: Kit Clash
events.body: Both teams arrive in almost identical colors. The supporters demand the right to design an emergency strip.

outcomes.text: The lightning-and-turnip pattern becomes an instant cult classic.
The winning design has seventeen colors and cannot legally be printed.
The match proceeds. The laundry manager receives a quiet round of applause.

events.title: Rat in the Trophy Cabinet
events.body: A very confident rat has moved into the empty space reserved for future silverware.

outcomes.text: The rat poses for photos in a tiny blazer and doubles museum attendance.
It steals the ticket float and retires under the west stand.
The rat accepts a transfer to the groundskeeper's shed.

events.title: Hero Exposé
events.body: The local paper wants a behind-the-scenes day with the club's most unusual players.

outcomes.text: The feature is warm, funny, and shared everywhere. Sponsors start calling before breakfast.
The headline focuses entirely on the dressing-room fire extinguisher budget.
The captain says all the right things and only one slightly strange thing.

events.title: The Goal Goes Viral
events.body: A blurry clip of last weekend's goal has reached three million views and one confused astronomy forum.

outcomes.text: The remix becomes a terrace anthem. Even the referee hums it.
The assistant coach's dance becomes the only part anyone remembers.
The supporters appreciate the message and ask for fewer hashtags next time.

events.title: Pundit Slams Your Tactics
events.body: A television pundit calls your formation 'a cupboard falling down a staircase.'

outcomes.text: Your magnetic-board demonstration wins the studio and becomes the clip of the week.
The magnets fall off. One rolls under the host's chair and remains there all segment.

choices.label: Pin it on the team-room wall

outcomes.text: The squad uses the quote as motivation and improves the cupboard.

events.title: A Pop-up Sponsor
events.body: A local mattress shop offers quick cash if the team celebrates the next win by pretending to nap.

outcomes.text: The synchronized celebration is perfect. Mattress sales and club shirts both surge.
The team performs it after a draw. Nobody is certain whether the sponsor still owes you.
Bert files the offer under SOMETIMES MONEY IS TOO STRANGE.

events.title: Your Hero Gets a Commercial
events.body: The sponsor wants a hero to advertise cereal by blasting open an indestructible breakfast box.

outcomes.text: The box explodes into harmless golden flakes. The catchphrase is on every playground by Monday.
The box survives. The spoon does not. The sponsor still pays the appearance fee.
The hero says 'crunch' with tremendous authority.

events.title: A Player in a Slump
events.body: One player stays behind after training, taking the same tired shot again and again.

outcomes.text: Shooting through a cardboard dragon works. The whole squad demands a turn.
The dragon falls over before the first shot. At least everyone laughs.
A day away from the noise restores some perspective.

events.title: Homesick Youth
events.body: A young player admits they miss home, their dog, and a very specific bakery.

outcomes.text: The family, dog, and bakery arrive together. The whole club adopts the pastry.
The dog steals the tactics board. Training becomes an unusually joyful chase.
The player returns smiling and carrying enough pastries for the bench.

events.title: A Player Wins the Lottery
events.body: A squad member arrives in a limousine that is far too long for the training-ground car park.

outcomes.text: They buy a recovery lounge and insist every chair has a name.
They buy a golden foghorn. It is powerful, useless, and now part of warmups.
The limousine is returned. The player keeps one tasteful velvet tracksuit.

events.title: Two Players Feud
events.body: Two lockers are now separated by a line of cones and a handwritten border checkpoint.

choices.label: Enter them in a duet challenge

outcomes.text: Their terrible club anthem wins the room and the border checkpoint comes down.
They argue about the chorus. Bert confiscates the microphone.
They cooperate long enough to move a giant tire and forget the original argument.

events.title: Agent Whispers
events.body: An agent has been seen measuring curtains in the away dressing room and complimenting your best players.

choices.label: Feed the agent a ridiculous rumor

outcomes.successHeadline: They scouted a player who does not exist
outcomes.text: Rivals waste a week scouting your fictional seven-foot winger. Your squad finds it hilarious.
The rumor appears in print with your name attached. The agent sends flowers.
The dressing room closes ranks and the curtain measurements stop.

events.title: Flu Wave
events.body: Half the squad sounds like a brass band tuning up inside a cupboard.

outcomes.text: The soup clears every nose and one blocked drain. Training resumes by lunch.
It is mostly pepper. Everyone can breathe, but nobody can stop crying.
The club closes for a quiet recovery day and comes back steadier.

events.title: The Miracle Physio
events.body: A traveling physio offers a one-day clinic using tape, tuning forks, and a small gong.

outcomes.text: The gong rings and the treatment room empties at a jog. Nobody understands it.
The gong startles the kit manager and achieves little else.
The physio writes a sensible report with no musical notation.

events.title: Ultras Want Cheaper Tickets
events.body: The supporters' group arrives with a banner, a spreadsheet, and surprisingly good handwriting.

outcomes.successHeadline: Scarves enough to wrap the stand
outcomes.text: The ground fills with families, songs, and enough scarves to wrap the stand twice.
Rain arrives sideways. The few who stay sing even louder.
The banner comes down and the spreadsheet receives a respectful nod from Bert.

events.title: A Kid Asks for a Hero
events.body: A handwritten letter asks whether a club hero can visit the local school and rescue sports day.

choices.label: Let the hero run sports day

outcomes.text: The hero loses the egg-and-spoon race on purpose and wins every heart in the playground.
One enthusiastic demonstration launches the beanbag onto the roof. The children call it brilliant.
The class sends back a team photo and thirty-seven tactical suggestions.

events.title: The Hundredth Fan
events.body: The ticket system identifies supporter number one hundred. They are extremely surprised by the marching band.

outcomes.text: The tiny parade blocks one roundabout and gains the club hundreds of curious followers.
The band arrives at the wrong house. That household becomes supporters anyway.
The supporter promises to bring ninety-nine friends eventually.

events.title: The Training Drone
events.body: A sponsor demo drone starts collecting cones, bibs, and anything else that stops moving.

choices.label: Turn it into a pressing drill

outcomes.text: The squad learns to swarm the drone and wins back every bib in record time.
The drone escapes with the captain's boot and invoices the club for delivery.
The sponsor apologizes and sends a box of normal, non-flying cones.

events.title: The Scoreboard Predicts Tomorrow
events.body: At midnight the scoreboard displays a result for a match that has not happened yet.

outcomes.text: Every predicted moment arrives. The club's preparation looks like magic.
The display was tomorrow's maintenance date. The tactical session becomes a useful laugh.
It continues glowing for six seconds, then behaves perfectly forever.

events.title: The Community Mural
events.body: Local artists offer to paint the stadium wall if the club supplies paint and one brave subject.

outcomes.text: The finished mural seems to move in the evening light. Supporters make it a match-day landmark.
Rain turns the hero into a purple cloud. The artists promise this is still powerful.
The crisp new crest becomes the most photographed wall in the district.

events.title: The First Win
events.body: The weekend result sheet is pinned to the office door. Somebody has drawn a small crown on it.

outcomes.successHeadline: The crown stays on the door
outcomes.text: Half the town squeezes in, the crowned sheet goes behind glass, and the squad walks taller all week.
The urn runs dry after nine cups. Everyone stays anyway and drinks squash.
Ten minutes of noise, then cones. The squad likes that you kept it short.

events.title: A Hero Finally Scores
events.body: The goal your hero has been threatening all season arrives, and three phones catch it from three useless angles.

outcomes.successHeadline: Three bad angles, one great goal
outcomes.text: Supporters stitch the shaky clips into one and the club account gains a following it did not earn.
All three angles are mostly the back of one steward's head. The steward is thrilled.
A printed still goes up with the date underlined twice. It stays there all season.

events.title: Three Goals Clear
events.body: The supporters' group has already printed a banner about the margin. It is enormous and slightly damp.

outcomes.successHeadline: Every visiting side reads it first
outcomes.text: Visiting teams walk out under it all season and the terrace never lets them forget the number.
It falls on the referee during the warm-up. He takes it surprisingly well.

choices.label: Keep it for a bigger day

outcomes.text: It is folded into the store cupboard and labelled FOR LATER, WHEN IT MEANS MORE.

events.title: Four Without Losing
events.body: A regional broadcaster wants two minutes on how a club this small stopped losing.

choices.label: Explain exactly how you did it

outcomes.text: You give the entire plan away on air. It works anyway, and everyone wants to watch the club that says the quiet part.
Three managers copy the plan by Tuesday. Two of them do it better.

choices.label: Credit the squad and stop talking

outcomes.text: You name all eighteen of them, slowly, until the segment runs out of time.

events.title: Through to the Next Round
events.body: The cup tie is won and the scoreboard operator has left the final score up all week on purpose.

choices.label: Leave the score up until the next round

outcomes.successHeadline: Nobody touched the switch for a week
outcomes.text: Supporters detour past the ground just to look at it. The next opponent arrives and reads it twice.
A storm knocks out the second digit. It now reads a much stranger result.

choices.label: Reset it and get back to the league

outcomes.text: The operator photographs it, then resets it, then photographs it again.

events.title: A Thousand Voices
events.body: The turnstile counter passes a thousand and the man who operates it insists on a photograph with it.

choices.label: Open the far side of the ground

outcomes.text: The far terrace fills, learns its own songs by half time, and starts answering the main stand.
Eleven people spread themselves across four hundred seats and enjoy the room.
The photograph goes in the programme. He buys forty copies for relatives.

events.title: The Push Is Real
events.body: Someone has started painting the season's results down the tunnel wall, one match at a time, in club colors.

choices.label: Let them paint the rest of the season

outcomes.successHeadline: The wall runs out of room
outcomes.text: The wall fills faster than the painter expected and the squad checks it on the way out every single day.
Two draws in a row get painted a suspicious shade of green. Nobody comments.

choices.label: Ask them to wait for May

outcomes.text: The painter agrees, then quietly primes the whole wall ready for one very good afternoon.

events.title: A Rival Bids
events.body: A club two divisions up has put a real number on one of your players and given you eight days to think about it.

choices.label: Tell them he is not for sale

outcomes.successHeadline: The answer travels faster than the bid
outcomes.text: Your flat refusal reaches the dressing room before it reaches their chairman. He decides you meant it about all of them.
Their scout keeps turning up anyway, now with a folding chair.

choices.label: Ask to hear the whole offer

outcomes.text: The number is better than you feared and the deadline is real. Bert writes both on the back of a teamsheet.

events.title: Deadline Day
events.body: The rival's final offer expires at five. Their chairman has phoned three times and left the same message.

outcomes.text: Five o'clock passes in total silence. He stays, signs nothing, and plays like a man who was wanted and chose here.
The offer expires and so does his good mood. He asks, politely, to be told next time.
The money lands the same afternoon. The squad understands the arithmetic and hates it politely.

events.title: Two Clubs, One Signature
events.body: The winger you have watched all month is sitting in a cafe with a rival's scout and a second, untouched coffee.

outcomes.text: You take the second chair, match the offer to the pound, and he signs a napkin before the rival returns from the counter.
He thanks you both, chooses neither, and moves to a club by the sea.
Your scout spends the afternoon on someone cheaper and, he insists, better.

events.title: An Unexpected Cheque
events.body: The kit sponsor has done better than expected this quarter and wants to share it, loudly, in front of a camera.

outcomes.successHeadline: It took four people to hold it
outcomes.text: The cheque is the size of a door. The photograph runs everywhere and the sponsor asks about next year before lunch.
The wind takes it across the car park. The money is fine; the cheque is not.

choices.label: Ask them to just wire it

outcomes.text: It arrives by Thursday with a note reading THANKS FOR NOT MAKING US HOLD A CHEQUE.

events.title: Best Pitch in the Division
events.body: The groundskeeper has won a small regional award and is pretending very hard not to care about it.

choices.label: Walk him round the pitch at half time

outcomes.successHeadline: He waved with the wrong hand the whole way
outcomes.text: He walks the full lap, waves with the wrong hand throughout, and the ground stands up for him twice.
He refuses to leave the mower shed and accepts the applause through a window.

choices.label: Spend the prize on new tools

outcomes.text: He returns with equipment nobody can name and a pitch that plays a yard faster.

events.title: A Club Legend Walks In
events.body: A man who played four hundred games here in the seventies is standing in reception holding his own boots.

choices.label: Ask him to take a session

outcomes.successHeadline: One drill, forty years old, still works
outcomes.text: He runs one drill he has sworn by since 1974. It is baffling, exhausting, and by Friday the squad asks for it again.
He mostly tells stories. Excellent stories, and a warm afternoon for everyone.

choices.label: Put the boots in the cabinet

outcomes.text: The boots go on the middle shelf. He visits every other Saturday to check on them.

events.title: The Kid Who Never Misses
events.body: The youth coach has waited outside your office for an hour to tell you about one player and one number.

choices.label: Put him in with the first team

outcomes.successHeadline: The number was not a typo
outcomes.text: He does it again in front of everyone, twice, and the senior squad quietly starts staying behind to watch.
He is nineteen and it shows for ninety minutes. He learns more in that hour than in a month.

choices.label: Leave him where he is winning

outcomes.text: The youth coach is delighted, which is rare, and hands over a session plan built around him.

events.title: The Saturday Radio Hour
events.body: Local radio wants an hour of build-up from the ground itself, with supporters allowed to phone in.

outcomes.text: Caller after caller says something kind and specific. The hour overruns and nobody at the station minds.
One caller talks for eleven minutes about parking. He is, in fairness, correct.

choices.label: Keep it to a match preview

outcomes.text: A tidy, useful hour. Two hundred people learn where the ground actually is.

events.title: Nobody in the Treatment Room
events.body: For the first time this season the physio has nothing to do and is visibly unsettled by it.

choices.label: Use the full squad while you have it

outcomes.successHeadline: Eighteen fit players in one session
outcomes.text: A whole squad in one session for once. The shape finally looks like the shape on the board.
Someone pulls up in the last ten minutes. The physio looks almost relieved.
They come back on Thursday looking like a different team, in the good way.

events.title: The West Stand Leaks
events.body: Four rows of the west stand are now officially a water feature. The safety officer has used the word CLOSED.

choices.label: Patch it with whoever turns up

outcomes.successHeadline: Nine supporters and one long ladder
outcomes.text: Nine supporters, one ladder, and a Sunday. The roof holds, and everyone who helped now owns a small piece of the ground.
The patch survives one shower. A professional is called, and charges for the diagnosis too.
It costs what it costs and is finished by Friday, dry and entirely unremarkable.

events.title: The West Stand Reopens
events.body: The dry rows go back on sale and the supporters who fixed them want the first four seats.

choices.label: Name the rows after the ladder crew

outcomes.successHeadline: Four seats with nine names on them
outcomes.text: Nine names go on a brass strip along four seats. Every one of them brings somebody new the following week.
The engraver misspells two names. Both men decide they prefer the new versions.

choices.label: Just put them back on sale

outcomes.text: They sell out in a morning, mostly to people who now check the roof out of habit.

events.title: A Choir on the Terrace
events.body: Six supporters have started singing in something close to harmony and are asking for a microphone.

outcomes.text: Six voices become sixty by half time. The terrace has a sound now, and it is genuinely quite good.
They attempt a key nobody can reach. The attempt itself becomes the joke of the season.
They sing anyway, all afternoon, and are hoarse and happy by full time.

events.title: The Anthem Gets a Verse
events.body: The terrace choir has written a second verse. It is about the club's plumbing and it is four minutes long.

outcomes.successHeadline: Four minutes about a boiler, charting locally
outcomes.text: The full version is released unedited and charts locally. The boiler becomes the most famous appliance in the county.
Four minutes proves to be three minutes too many. The chorus survives; the verse does not.
The trimmed chorus is sung on the way out of every home game from then on.
